short: 338,000 men lifted from a French beach after the Allied front in the west collapsed.
full:
The German armoured thrust through the Ardennes reached the Channel at Abbeville on 20 May 1940, cutting off the British Expeditionary Force, the French First Army and the Belgians in Flanders. Operation Dynamo began on 26 May, with the Royal Navy expecting to lift perhaps 45,000 men. A German halt order between 24 and 26 May, together with the French defence of Lille, bought time, and Goering's assurance that the Luftwaffe could finish the pocket by itself was not made good.

Destroyers took men off the mole in Dunkirk harbour while some 700 little ships ferried others from the beaches. By 4 June 338,226 troops had been evacuated, around a third of them French. All the heavy equipment was left behind: nearly 2,500 guns and 65,000 vehicles. Nine destroyers and more than 200 other vessels were lost. It was a defeat, and wars are not won by evacuations, but the army that fought from 1942 onwards was largely the army rescued in 1940.
